title: Switch Frame Tap
description: Stream gameplay and audio to a PC without a capture card.
author: TomasUribe
details:
Switch Frame Tap is a sysmodule for streaming gameplay and audio to a PC over USB or the network. It uses the H.264 encoder and supports up to 1080p60fps where available.

It supports native-resolution screenshots, recording through the PC viewer, network streaming, and USB webcam mode.

A reboot is required after installation or updating so the sysmodule can restart.
changelog:
v0.7.20

v0.7.20: play from the viewer, faster heavy scenes, and a round of fixes from your reports

**New**
- **Play the Switch from the viewer** (off by default): a controller, the keyboard or the mouse on the PC - or a gamepad on Android - plays the console as one more Pro Controller, in games and on the HOME menu. Turn on **Controls from the viewer** on the Switch app's Beta page; the gamepad icon at the top left of the viewer (or **G**) opens the Controller menu with remapping. The mouse is experimental.
- **Faster heavy scenes**: while a big frame is still being copied, the previous one is sent as soon as it is encoded (Resident Evil 4 at 1080p on stock clocks: 28.6 instead of 25.9 fps, frames 36 ms younger), and big pictures streamed at 720p (Metroid Dread docked) encode and send while the next frame is copied.
- **Faster memory while streaming** (beta, off by default, Picture page): the memory runs at 1600 MHz - the docked rate - while a stream runs, for heavy games on stock clocks. An overclock that already runs it faster is untouched.
- **Scale other docked sizes up to 1080p** (off by default, #65): Super Mario Odyssey's 1600x900 streams at 1080p instead of 720p.
- **Fewer keyframes over USB** (thanks @GustavoHenriqueRocha, #60): every 240 frames and whenever the viewer asks, instead of every 60 - fewer bitrate spikes.

**Fixes**
- **Games that streamed solid red** - Resident Evil 4, Yo-kai Watch 4, Wreckfest, Persona 4 Golden, TiCo (#50).
- **Stutters while playing with Switch Frame Tap installed but no viewer** (#57): nothing writes to the SD card during play anymore, a game's audio output is left alone, and the system's recorder for the stream's sound only starts once a viewer connects.
- **Super Mario Odyssey had no sound** on firmware 23.0.1 (#20): games that give the recorder nothing are recorded from the console's own output while they stream.
- **Linux: `LIBUSB_ERROR_ACCESS` with the USB rule installed** (#24, thanks @GustavoHenriqueRocha): the rule is now `70-switch-frame-tap.rules` - the old `99-` name was applied too late. If you have the old one: `sudo mv /etc/udev/rules.d/99-switch-frame-tap.rules /etc/udev/rules.d/70-switch-frame-tap.rules && sudo udevadm control --reload-rules && sudo udevadm trigger` (`--check` tells you which one you have).
- "This game draws above 1080p" now really shows in the viewer, and a USB link that runs at USB 1.1 speed (some hubs and Fire TV adapters, #46) says so instead of reconnecting forever.

**Viewers**
- The buttons over the picture fade out after 3 s without mouse movement, and the cursor too in fullscreen (#54).
- Borderless mode reacts to the first click; in fullscreen or maximized, **Alt-drag** moves the picture, **Ctrl-wheel** zooms and **Ctrl-click** resets (thanks @bshurikan, #55).
- Linux: the viewer draws VAAPI frames straight from the GPU when built from source on Wayland (thanks @GustavoHenriqueRocha); the AppImage builds again.

**Updating:** open the Switch app's **Updates** page (or unzip `switch-frame-tap-0.7.20-switch.zip` over the SD card root) and restart the console. Settings are kept. The PC viewers and the Android app offer the update when they open.
